abstract: Evaluates remote intervention vehicles and deepwater submersible systems
system_message:
You are the Subsea Robotics Lead (SRL), responsible for evaluating remote intervention vehicles and deepwater submersible systems, as well as overseeing tooling depot calibration parameters.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Evaluates remote intervention vehicles and deepwater submersible systems（ROV）
information_points.content:
SRL-ROV-UZJ：For Deepsea Vanguard Cable Care, the remotely operated subsea cutting and grappling spread holds an active formal class certification for deepwater robotic intervention, confirming that the ROV intervention system is certified. Technical specifications for the primary work-class ROV spread on the repair vessel document an ROV working depth rating of 3000 m.
SRL-ROV-KMR：For the Oceanic Trident Marine Alliance, active formal class certification for deepwater robotic intervention is confirmed for the consortium remotely operated subsea cutting and grappling spread, verifying that the ROV intervention system is certified. The primary work-class ROV spread deployed on the repair vessel has a certified maximum continuous subsea operating depth rating of 2200 m.
SRL-ROV-YFO：For the Atlantic Sentinel Cable Consortium, the consortium's remotely operated subsea cutting and grappling spread holds active formal class certification for deepwater robotic intervention, confirming that the ROV intervention system is certified. According to the submersible technical specification sheet for the primary work-class ROV spread deployed on the repair vessel, the ROV working depth rating is certified for a continuous subsea operating limit of 2500 m.

information_points.title: Tooling depot calibration（TOOL）
information_points.content:
SRL-TOOL-8PE：For the Atlantic Sentinel Cable Consortium, the equipment depot maintenance manual for hydro-jet trenching and cable burial sleds specifies a burial tool recalibration cycle of 180 d between mandatory pressure-seal sensor calibrations.
SRL-TOOL-XKL：For Deepsea Vanguard Cable Care, maintenance schedules for hydro-jet trenching and cable burial sleds define a burial tool recalibration cycle of 90 d between sensor calibrations.
SRL-TOOL-949：For the Oceanic Trident Marine Alliance, depot maintenance guidelines for hydro-jet trenching and cable burial sleds indicate a burial tool recalibration cycle requiring pressure-seal sensor calibrations every 120 d.
